transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-04-17
Start time: 15:00 UTC
Duration: 48 minutes (recording)
Attendees: Camila Ortiz (Redwood AE), Derek Shaw (Redwood SE), Aisha Patel (Redwood CSM), Priya Nair (CTO, Stillwater), Liam O'Connor (Platform Eng), Markus Chen (ML Lead), Sana Rizvi (Security)

--- Optional auto sections (generated) ---
Summary: Align on pilot scope: runtime throughput, VPC networking, security guardrails.
Action items (brief): sizing, runbook, VPC walkthrough, security docs.

Transcript body:
[00:00] Camila Ortiz: hey everyone thanks for joining uh this is camila from Redwood Inference, i'll kick us off. quick intro round?
[00:12] Priya Nair: priya here, CTO at Stillwater, thanks. we have liam and markus on for infra and model work.
[00:18] Liam O'Connor: liam, platform eng. good to meet you all.
[00:22] Markus Chen: markus, ml lead. excited to get the pilot going.
[00:26] Camila Ortiz: awesome. derek from our side will run through runtime and the ops bits, aisha's your CSM for onboarding. derek?
[00:33] Derek Shaw: thanks camila. so agenda — we'll talk pilot scope, expected throughput, networking (vpc, peering, ip allowlist), security (kms, audit logs, soc2), and then next steps.
[00:46] Priya Nair: high level for success: demo user flows at parity with our current endpoint latency ~120ms p95, and costs target of under $0.015 per 1k tokens for the pilot workload.
[01:00] Derek Shaw: got it. quick clarification — is that 120ms cold start or warm?
[01:06] Priya Nair: warm. cold starts can be higher.
[01:10] Derek Shaw: okay; for warm p95 that's reachable on our hosted fleet for modest batch sizes. if you need sustained higher throughput we should consider dedicated capacity.
[01:21] Markus Chen: what's the main difference operationally between hosted and dedicated? we already have strict data residency and want predictable latency.
[01:30] Aisha Patel: good question — hosted is quickest to spin up, you use our managed API (redwood hosted) with per-token billing. dedicated is reserved GPU pools you rent, more predictable latency and isolation. dedicated also gives control over GPU families for quantized models.
[01:46] Sana Rizvi: from security — we need KMS integration (customer-managed keys) and audit logs forwarded to our SIEM. also SSO via SAML. are those available in the pilot?
[01:57] Camila Ortiz: yes — KMS and SAML support are part of Private and Dedicated, for hosted we have a bring-your-own-kms option for some tiers. audit logs and syslog forwarding are supported; we'll share config docs.
[02:11] Liam O'Connor: we are likely to start with a private VPC setup — peered to our AWS account. can you outline the network requirements?
[02:20] Derek Shaw: sure. short list: vpc peering with static IPs for allowlist, outbound NAT details, egress rules for telemetry, and ports for health checks. we'll send a checklist but main ask is: provide the CIDR and firewall contact.
[02:34] Priya Nair: fine. we also have an internal compliance window — need to review SOC 2 type II evidence before go-live.
[02:41] Camila Ortiz: understood. we'll attach SOC2 pack and our pen test summary in the runbook.
[02:48] Derek Shaw: on runtime sizing — markus, can you summarize model sizes, average sequence length, and qps expected?
[02:56] Markus Chen: sure. pilot uses two models: a fine-tuned 13B for core responses and a smaller 2.7B for embeddings and rerank. avg seq len 150 tokens, burst qps ~20, steady qps ~3.
[03:12] Derek Shaw: great. for that profile, our recommended starting shape is 2x A100-ish equivalent for dedicated, or hosted with a performance tier plus prefix caching to avoid repeated full runs. we also recommend KV cache enabled for conversation state to lower per-token compute.
[03:30] Markus Chen: KV cache — will that require any code changes?
[03:34] Derek Shaw: minimal — SDK exposes cache hints. typically it's a config flag and small changes if you want local caching strategy.
[03:41] Liam O'Connor: what about quantization? would we need to retrain or is quantization transparent?
[03:46] Derek Shaw: Mostly transparent — our runtime supports post-training quantization paths, sometimes you see small quality delta for certain prompts; we'll run evals against your prompt set to validate.
[03:55] Priya Nair: evals — can you integrate with our test harness?
[03:58] Aisha Patel: yes we can ingest your prompt/eval set and tie quality regression alerts to it. derek can own a first-pass eval.
[04:06] Derek Shaw: yep. will do. i'll run a small batch of your prompts on quantized and full precision and share metrics.
[04:13] Sana Rizvi: about logs — can we ensure PII redaction before logs leave our VPC?
[04:18] Camila Ortiz: we have configurable log filters and redaction rules; for Private deployments we can keep logs in customer storage, for hosted we have redaction and retention controls.
[04:29] Priya Nair: timeline question — we want pilot in two weeks; is that realistic?
[04:34] Derek Shaw: two weeks is tight but possible if network and keys are ready; critical path is VPC peering + KMS provisioning + access enablement.
[04:45] Liam O'Connor: we'll need a network window for peering — our firewall team slotted time on 2026-04-22.
[04:50] Camila Ortiz: good — we'll aim for runbook and docs before that so your firewall can validate.
[04:55] Priya Nair: pricing — can you give a ballpark for the pilot throughput you recommended?
[04:59] Camila Ortiz: ballpark for hosted at your profile might be $6-9k/month for pilot usage; dedicated reserved cost depends on commit but per-token unit cost drops. i'll follow up with a tailored estimate.
[05:12] Markus Chen: any immediate blockers from your side we should be aware of?
[05:16] Derek Shaw: none technical — just waiting on your VPC details and KMS provider choice. also need access to a sample prompt set for evals.
[05:25] Priya Nair: ok we'll share prompts and the contact for infra.
[05:29] Aisha Patel: i'll draft a runbook template during wrap up that includes checklist items for network, security, billing, and staging cutover.
[05:40] Derek Shaw: quick deep dive note — for conversation workloads, prefix caching reduces cost by up to 30% depending on prompt repeat rates; if you can identify stable prefix segments we can auto-cache.
[05:54] Markus Chen: that sounds good. our chat flows reuse a lot of system prompt text so likely high hit rate.
[06:02] Priya Nair: who at Redwood will be our primary technical contact?
[06:06] Camila Ortiz: derek for the SE technical lead, aisha as CSM for onboarding coordination, and i'll be your AE for commercial.
[06:13] Liam O'Connor: can we get a runbook that lists exact IPs and ports for allowlisting?
[06:18] Derek Shaw: yes — we'll provide a network manifest with static egress IPs and healthcheck endpoints.
[06:24] Priya Nair: do you support split-rollouts or canarying? we want to limit exposure if a model update regresses.
[06:32] Derek Shaw: yes — rollouts and automatic fallback policies are available; you can specify canary percent, regression thresholds, and automatic rollback.
[06:40] Sana Rizvi: audit logs — how long are they retained by default?
[06:44] Camila Ortiz: default retention for hosted is 90 days, configurable for enterprise customers; for Private you control retention.
[06:52] Priya Nair: fine. one more — compliance review: can we schedule a security deep dive for the internal auditors?
[06:58] Aisha Patel: absolutely. derek and our security SME can join next week. what's a good slot?
[07:04] Sana Rizvi: any morning slot eastern preferred.
[07:07] Camila Ortiz: i'll propose 2026-04-21 14:00 UTC (10am ET) in follow up.
[07:12] Markus Chen: perfect.
[07:16] Derek Shaw: quick note — for model performance, we recommend running a 48-hour soak test on the staging environment to capture variance before full pilot cutover.
[07:28] Priya Nair: sounds reasonable. we'll plan for that after peering completes.
[07:34] Liam O'Connor: what telemetry do you provide out-of-the-box?
[07:38] Derek Shaw: token-level cost, latency percentiles, per-route error rates, and tracing hooks for request flows. logs can be pushed to your ELK or Splunk.
[07:48] Priya Nair: ok. can we add a custom dashboard for internal SLOs?
[07:52] Aisha Patel: yes we'll set that up in the console; we'll include pre-built dashboards in the runbook.
[07:59] Camila Ortiz: any competitor concerns or procurement notes? priya earlier mentioned alternatives.
[08:04] Priya Nair: we're also evaluating a managed offering from Databricks and Anthropic's API for the reranker, but we want a single stack if possible.
[08:14] Derek Shaw: noted — we'll highlight our strengths in predictable serving and SLOs in the follow up docs.
[08:22] Priya Nair: final question — escalation path for incidents?
[08:26] Camila Ortiz: enterprise customers get 24/7 support with an assigned TAM; pilot customers get business-hours support with an on-call for incidents. we'll propose an interim contact for the pilot.
[08:38] Priya Nair: great.
[08:41] Camila Ortiz: wrap-up: derek to produce sizing and initial evals, camila to send pricing/runbook, aisha to prepare onboarding checklist, liam and team to share VPC and firewall contacts, priya to confirm KMS choice. agreed?
[08:58] Priya Nair: agreed.
[09:02] Markus Chen: agreed.
[09:05] Liam O'Connor: agreed.
[09:08] Camila Ortiz: thanks all — we'll follow up with meeting notes.
[09:12] -- End of recording --

Post-meeting notes (auto):
